datasets.title: Synthetic smart-contract security relations
datasets.description: Synthetic smart-contract security corpus for testing x402 clients: graph retrieval over a fictional SWC-style audit corpus, with source excerpts. Fiction, kept as a test fixture, not a product. For real work use the retraction SKUs on /api/v1/judge.

datasets.title: Retraction propagation judgment
datasets.description: Check one paper for retraction, and whether that retraction reaches the references it builds on. Send a DOI or paper ID; get a verdict (CONTESTED / SUPPORTED / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE), the retracted papers it depends on with per-source status and date, and an explicit abstention instead of a guess when coverage is thin. Snapshot updated 2026-10-25: 98,868 papers, 572 retraction assertions. Deterministic verdict path, no LLM. $0.02 per call.

datasets.title: Retraction evidence audit
datasets.description: The same retraction check as the $0.02 call, plus the full evidence trail: every citation hop with its source tier and URI, the context class (acknowledges the retraction / critical / supporting / neutral), cross-source conflict flags, and a deterministic written explanation. Use it when the answer has to survive review: journal screening, grant and tenure files, due diligence on a cited claim. Snapshot updated 2026-10-25. $0.10 per call.

datasets.title: Reference list audit - 10 references
datasets.description: Audit a bibliography: up to 10 references in one call, each DOI string or full citation line. For every item you get the matched paper, its retraction status from OpenAlex and Retraction Watch (Crossref when an update-to notice exists) with tier and date, the retracted papers it depends on, and an explicit unmatched list for anything not in the snapshot. One x402 payment and one round trip instead of ten. Snapshot updated 2026-10-25: 98,868 papers, 572 retraction assertions.

datasets.title: Dependency vulnerability scan - 20 packages
datasets.description: Check up to 20 package@version entries for known vulnerabilities in one call. Send packages as strings ("lodash@4.17.20") or objects ({name, version, ecosystem}); supported ecosystems: npm (default), PyPI, Go, crates.io, Maven, NuGet, RubyGems, Packagist. Each entry comes back with affected yes or no, the advisory IDs and their CVE aliases, a severity label, the fixed versions, and the source URL. Advisories come from OSV; a package with no advisory is reported as no known advisory, never as safe. $0.02 per call.
